quiz_result_body_curiosity: Your strength is Curiosity. You seek to understand things deeply. The flip side: information overload, mental fatigue, and overanalyzing instead of feeling. We will help turn mental processing into direct somatic awareness and emotional clarity.
quiz_result_body_kindness: Your strength is Kindness. The flip side: a tendency to burn out while saving others, ignoring your own body's signals. We will teach you to direct that same care toward yourself.
quiz_result_body_gratitude: Your strength is Gratitude. You naturally focus on the positive. The flip side: toxic positivity and suppressing painful emotions like anger or grief by telling yourself 'others have it worse.' We will give you a safe space to process difficult feelings without guilt.
quiz_result_body_hope: Your strength is Hope. You always look toward a brighter future. The flip side: waiting for things to get better while tolerating chronic stress and ignoring what hurts right now. We will help you ground yourself in the present and take action today.
quiz_result_body_wisdom: Your strength is Wisdom. You analyze what's happening around you deeply — but that can leave you stuck in rumination and anxiety. We will help turn that analysis into gentle self-observation, without the extra worry.
quiz_result_body_selfRegulation: Your strength is Self-regulation. You know how to hold steady under pressure. But constant self-control often leads to hidden physical tension and chronic stress. The app will help you safely release that pressure.
quiz_result_body_love: Your strength is Love. You form deep, meaningful connections. The flip side: fear of rejection, porous boundaries, and anxiety about losing others at the expense of your own needs. We will help you build solid inner security so you can love without losing yourself.
quiz_result_body_humor: Your strength is Humor. You effortlessly lighten the mood. The flip side: using laughter and sarcasm as an emotional shield to avoid vulnerability, pain, or fear. We will provide the tools to safely acknowledge and release the tension you mask with humor.

cognitive_distortions_warm_note: This is a very common thinking pattern — you're not alone in it. We'll work through it together next.
cognitive_distortion_all_or_nothing_thin: Everything is seen in extremes, with no middle ground
If it's not perfect, it's a total failure
cognitive_distortion_overgeneralization_: One event is seen as an endless pattern
This always happens. Nothing ever works out
cognitive_distortion_mental_filter_defin: Only the negative is noticed, the positive is ignored
cognitive_distortion_disqualifying_posit: Good things are explained away as luck, not your own doing
I just got lucky. It doesn't count
cognitive_distortion_mind_reading_defini: Being certain you know what others are thinking
cognitive_distortion_mind_reading_exampl: He definitely thinks I'm a failure
cognitive_distortion_fortune_telling_def: Being certain of a negative outcome with no evidence
cognitive_distortion_fortune_telling_exa: It's not going to work out anyway
cognitive_distortion_catastrophizing_def: A minor event is blown up into a catastrophe
cognitive_distortion_catastrophizing_exa: This is the end of everything
cognitive_distortion_emotional_reasoning: A feeling is taken as fact
I feel guilty, so I must be guilty
cognitive_distortion_should_statements_d: Rigid demands on yourself or the world using "should/must"
cognitive_distortion_labeling_definition: A mistake becomes a personality trait
cognitive_distortion_labeling_example: I'm an idiot (instead of "I made a mistake")
cognitive_distortion_personalization_def: Taking excessive personal responsibility for things outside your control
cognitive_distortion_personalization_exa: It's my fault everything went wrong

its_not_about_great_dreams:
This isn't about big dreams, goals, or races — just the simplest desires.

Desires are about simple things. This exercise helps you learn to hear yourself and your true desires.

Write down what you love or like, and what you want.
What exactly?

What do I want right now? Some small thing, here and now.
I want to drink/lie down/sit/sleep, fish, an apple, a movie, a book — anything, and exactly what.
get_start_with_simple_things:
It starts with simple things, and the more you practice, the more deeply you start to look into and shape your own path.

Example: I want an apple right now, I want to cry right now, I want to drink, I want to listen to music.

insight_matrix_theory_body: Psychology splits emotions along two axes: how pleasant they are (valence) and how much physical energy they demand (activation). Anger and anxiety make the body produce cortisol and adrenaline — that drains your internal battery even while you're just sitting in a chair. Calm and solitude activate the parasympathetic system, which restores your strength.

insight_heatmap_nudge_1: The problem isn't the activity itself, it's the environment. What exactly about "{cond_bad}" causes the tension — could that factor be softened?
insight_heatmap_nudge_2: Try moving "{activity}" into "{cond_good}" conditions, where it's easier for you, even just as a trial.
insight_heatmap_theory_title: Why does environment matter so much?
insight_heatmap_theory_body: The brain forms reflexive links not just with tasks themselves but with the surroundings too. Lighting, noise, or the presence of specific people can quietly overload the nervous system — this is called sensory overload. Changing just one element of the environment (like noise-cancelling headphones) can noticeably shift your emotional reaction to a routine task.

insight_battery_summary: Your comfortable socializing limit right now is about {x}h. Past that point your mood tends to dip and irritability can appear. To fully recharge, your nervous system usually needs about {y}h alone.
insight_battery_theory_body: Any socializing — even with the people you love most — takes real work from the brain: reading micro-expressions, adjusting your tone, managing empathy. Under stress, that work exhausts people faster. Needing time alone isn't a sign you don't love the people around you — it's a basic physiological need to lower cognitive load.
